h: Love and Awe Mature Into the Rest of Shabbos

p: In the Minchah prayer of Shabbos we say,
כִּי הִנֵּה מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
For the middah of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
that is, an outpouring of love for Hashem Yisbarach
as in what is stated in the Rokeach:
there is no strength like piety at its beginning.
And it is stated in the holy Zohar:
כְּתִיב עִבְדוּ אֶת ה׳ בְּשִׂמְחָה (תְּהִלִּים ק, ב)
it is written, "Serve Hashem with joy" (Tehillim 100:2),
וּכְתִיב עִבְדוּ אֶת ה׳ בְּיִרְאָה (שָׁם ב, יא)
and it is written, "Serve Hashem with fear" (Tehillim 2:11);
here, when the Beis HaMikdash stands,
for then there is a revelation of Godliness,
and then joy spreads through the heart
the middah of Avraham Avinu, as mentioned above.
However, there is not yet a clarification
that the joy is from holiness,
except when yirah branches off from it,
כְּדְאִיתָא בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג)
as stated in Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu Rabbah (beginning of chapter 3):
וְלָזֶה נֶאֱמַר לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And therefore it was said to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
at the culmination of his clarification,
at the time of the Akeidah:
עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית כב, יב)
"Now I know that you fear God" (Bereishis 22:12);
for through the yirah it was clarified
retroactively that the joy and the love
And as we heard from our Rebbe,
עַל מַאֲמַר הַגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא מד, א)
on the statement of the Gemara (Bava Metzia 44a):
and now you go back and teach us in your old age
That is, in the days of childhood,
when longing is found in a person's heart,
out of the kindness of youth, for holiness,
and this is the aspect of silver;
but it is only for the purpose
that through it he acquire gold,
that is, to acquire in his soul the aspect of yirah,
which is alluded to by gold, as is known.
And in his old age he taught
that is, the ultimate clarification of yirah,
comes precisely when there comes from it
and this is "I rejoiced out of my fear."
And then the soul is completed in holiness entirely,
when there is completed in it the holiness
of the aspect of the three holy Avos.
And about this we say, "Avraham will exult":
כִּי גִּילָה הוּא הַשִּׂמְחָה בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הַלֵּב
for "gilah" is joy in the inwardness of the heart,
וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג לט, א)
and as stated in the holy Zohar (III 39a)
who are from the side of Chesed,
that wine was forbidden to them,
which is the matter of revealed joy,
but all their deeds are in silence.
for from the aspect of yirah
which is from the side of the Levi'im,
And therefore it says regarding Yitzchak,
וַיָּבֵא לוֹ יַיִן וַיֵּשְׁתְּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כז, כה)
"And he brought him wine, and he drank" (Bereishis 27:25)
for from fear are born exultation and joy.
"Yaakov and his sons will rest on it":
שֶׁבְּחִינַת קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for the aspect of the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
is after there were included in him
the two aspects, yirah and joy;
and then there is complete rest,
And this is at the third meal,
which is called "the Will of wills,"
after there has been acquired in us
the aspect of love and fear
וְעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ חֲזַ״ל (בֵּיצָה טז, א)
at the time the holiness of Shabbos departs;
when the ultimate holiness has been completed in us,
